# Dell SmartFabric OS10 — MIB Reference

## Provenance note

Unlike the original seven Tier-1 vendors, this vendor's MIB research was conducted via search-summary results and targeted page fetches (Dell's own documentation portal and a third-party MIB-browser mirror) rather than a full primary MIB-source read. Treat OID values below as "confirmed to exist at this location" where a source directly stated it, and as "plausible, needs live-device or full-document confirmation" everywhere else — the same discipline used throughout this docs tree, just applied to thinner source material for this vendor. See [`overview.md`](overview.md)'s closing uncertainty note.

## A genuine PEN ambiguity, documented rather than resolved

Two different Dell-associated Private Enterprise Numbers surfaced during this research, and they are **not interchangeable** — a future reader should not assume one supersedes the other without checking which hardware/firmware generation is in play:

- **PEN 674 ("Dell Inc.")** — Dell's own long-standing enterprise number. OS10's own product/enterprise MIB tree is confirmed rooted here: `DELLEMC-OS10-PRODUCTS-MIB`'s `os10Products` object is at `1.3.6.1.4.1.674.11000.5000.100.2` (confirmed via a third-party MIB-browser mirror — see [`mibs/README.md`](mibs/README.md)), i.e. the chain is `enterprises.674` → `11000` (Dell EMC OS10 products arc) → `5000` → `100` → `2`. A separate reference surfaced during this session (`1.3.6.1.4.1.674.11000.5000.200.1.1`, BGP-related) suggests `11000.5000` is a broader OS10-enterprise-MIB parent arc with multiple sibling branches (`.100.*` for chassis/product objects, `.200.*` for BGP, plausibly others not investigated this session) — worth confirming the full sibling list before treating `.100.2` as the only entry point.
- **PEN 6027 ("Force10 Networks")** — Dell's acquired Force10 heritage number. Search results this session associated `sysObjectID` values for specific PowerSwitch models (S3048-ON, S4048-ON, S6010-ON) with enterprise number 6027, not 674 — meaning **`sysObjectID`-based vendor/model auto-detection for at least some OS10-capable hardware may resolve under the legacy Force10 PEN, not Dell's own 674**, even though the device is running current OS10 software. This was not fully reconciled this session (i.e., it's unclear whether *all* OS10 hardware reports `sysObjectID` under 6027, or only specific model families, or only devices that started life on OS9/FTOS before an OS10 conversion).

**Practical implication for SignalScope**: per [`standard-mibs.md`](../../00-architecture/standard-mibs.md)'s "poll `sysObjectID` first" guidance, do not hardcode a single expected PEN for Dell/OS10 vendor auto-detection — check for **both** `1.3.6.1.4.1.674.*` and `1.3.6.1.4.1.6027.*` prefixes, and treat resolving this cleanly (which PEN which model/firmware combination actually reports) as an open item for the verification backlog in [`ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md).

## Standard (RFC/IEEE) MIBs supported

**Updated Phase 2 (2026-07-22) — first-hand-read, complete list.** Dell's own OS10 User Guide (Release 10.5.0, full PDF — see [`overview.md`](overview.md)'s sources) Table 5 lists exactly 22 standard MIBs, quoted in full here since this is now a primary-source-confirmed complete enumeration rather than a partial/inferred list:

`BRIDGE-MIB` (IEEE 802.1D) · `ENTITY-MIB` (RFC 6933) · `EtherLike-MIB` (RFC 3635) · `HOST-RESOURCES-MIB` (RFC 2790) · `IEEE8021-PFC-MIB` (IEEE 802.1Qbb) · `IEEE8023-LAG-MIB` (IEEE 802.3ad) · `IF-MIB` (RFC 2863) · `IP-FORWARD-MIB` (RFC 4292) · `IP-MIB` (RFC 4293) · `LLDP-EXT-DOT1-MIB` / `LLDP-EXT-DOT3-MIB` / `LLDP-MIB` (IEEE 802.1AB) · `OSPF-MIB` (RFC 4750) · `OSPFV3-MIB` (RFC 5643) · `Q-BRIDGE-MIB` (IEEE 802.1Q) · `RFC1213-MIB` · `SFLOW-MIB` (RFC 3176) · `SNMP-FRAMEWORK-MIB`/`SNMP-MPD-MIB`/`SNMP-NOTIFICATION-MIB`/`SNMP-TARGET-MIB`/`SNMP-USER-BASED-SM-MIB`/`SNMP-VIEW-BASED-ACM-MIB` (agent-framework MIBs, RFC 3411–3415) · `SNMPv2-MIB` (RFC 3418) · `TCP-MIB` (RFC 4022) · `UDP-MIB` (RFC 4113).

**Correction to a prior-session claim**: an earlier pass asserted Dell's OS10 User Guide states "partial implementations of RFC 4188 (BRIDGE-MIB) and RFC 4363 (Q-BRIDGE-MIB) are supported." **That sentence does not appear in the actual MIBs chapter** — verified by a full-text read of the PDF (`grep -i partial` across the complete converted text finds nothing MIB-related). Table 5 lists `BRIDGE-MIB`/`Q-BRIDGE-MIB` with no partial/full qualifier of any kind. **Retract the "partial implementation" claim** — it was very likely a search-engine-summary artifact from the earlier search-summary-only research pass, not real page content. `RMON-MIB` is genuinely absent from OS10's own list (not merely unconfirmed) — do not assume RMON support for this vendor. `LLDP-MIB`/`ENTITY-MIB` are now confirmed present (they were previously "expected but unverified").

## Confirmed vendor-specific behavior

- **Standard `BGP4-MIB` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.15`) returns "No such object" on OS10** — Dell's own documentation states OS10 uses the proprietary `DELLEMC-OS10-BGP4V2-MIB` instead. While BGP itself is a routing concern outside SignalScope's L2-switch-focused scope, this is a useful signal about OS10's general posture: **prefer checking for a Dell enterprise MIB before assuming standard-MIB coverage is complete**, more so than for the other six vendors researched with full primary-source access, where the standard-MIB baseline was more reliably confirmed protocol-by-protocol.
- `DELLEMC-OS10-PRODUCTS-MIB` (`os10Products`, `.674.11000.5000.100.2`) — **updated Phase 2 (2026-07-22)**: this module's full sibling-product enumeration is now confirmed (via the third-party Observium mirror, not first-hand MIB source — flag accordingly): `os10SSeriesProducts` (`.100.2.1`, containing `s6000on`/`s4048on`/`s4048Ton`/`s3048on`/`s6010on`/`s4128Ton`), `os10MSeriesProducts` (`.100.2.2`), `os10ZSeriesProducts` (`.100.2.3`), and `os10NSeriesProducts` (`.100.2.4`, containing `n3248TEon`) — i.e. this is purely a `sysObjectID`-style hardware-model identity tree (useful for SignalScope's vendor/model auto-detection, see [`data-model-notes.md`](../../00-architecture/data-model-notes.md)), **not** a configuration or inventory-table module in the `ENTITY-MIB::entPhysicalTable` sense. No chassis/module/PSU/fan table was found in this MIB — that data, if SNMP-exposed at all, is more likely under `DELLEMC-OS10-CHASSIS-MIB` (name confirmed via the official User Guide's Table 6, internal structure not enumerated).
- **OS10's enterprise MIB set is confirmed complete and thin**: exactly five modules (`DELLEMC-OS10-BGP4V2-MIB`, `DELLEMC-OS10-CHASSIS-MIB`, `DELLEMC-OS10-PRODUCTS-MIB`, `DELLEMC-OS10-SMI-MIB`, `DELLEMC-OS10-TC-MIB`), per Dell's own Table 6 — this is now a first-hand-confirmed complete list (Phase 2, 2026-07-22), not a partial/still-researching set. See the write-support section below for why this matters.

## SNMP write support

**Re-researched Phase 2 (2026-07-22) — moved from "research gap" to "verified absence of a documented write path," still no object confirmed writable.** Obtained and read the complete SNMP/MIBs chapter of Dell's own OS10 User Guide (see [`overview.md`](overview.md) for the PDF source and full reasoning). Key finding: **none of OS10's five enterprise MIBs is a configuration-action module** — there is no Dell/Force10 equivalent of Cisco's `CISCO-VLAN-MEMBERSHIP-MIB`/`CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB` or Aruba's `ARUBAWIRED-PORTSECURITY-MIB`/`ARUBAWIRED-CONFIG-MIB`/`ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB`. This is unlike every other full-tier vendor in this project, all of which have at least one enterprise MIB purpose-built for some config-write action.

This leaves only the standard-MIB path as a theoretical possibility: `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` and `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` are declared read-write in their base IETF MIB source (true for every vendor's implementation, not Dell-specific), but **no OS10-specific documentation confirms the agent honors a SET on either object**, and the User Guide's own summary phrasing — *"OS10 supports standard and private SNMP MIBs, including all get requests"* — conspicuously does not mention set requests (suggestive, not conclusive, and explicitly flagged as such rather than treated as proof of GET-only behavior). No SNMP path for trunk-allowed-VLAN, STP edge-port, port-security, LACP membership, or config-save/checkpoint was found or is plausible given the absence of any supporting enterprise MIB.

**Practical guidance unchanged**: per [`gui-cli-snmp-unification.md`](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md)'s standing rule, **treat every OS10 configuration action as CLI-only** (the `switchport`/`channel-group`/`spanning-tree`/`switchport port-security` commands in [`cli-reference.md`](cli-reference.md)). The evidentiary basis for that guidance is now much stronger than before — a first-hand read of Dell's complete MIB list, not an unresearched gap — see [`comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md`](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md) for the updated cross-vendor framing.

## Objects not confirmed this session

- Whether `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` or `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` actually accept a SET on live OS10 hardware despite no documentation either confirming or ruling it out — the one item that would require live-device access or a much deeper community/forum search to resolve further; not expected to change the CLI-only guidance even if eventually confirmed writable, given the complete absence of any GUI-relevant enterprise MIB.
- Which PEN (674 vs. 6027) a given OS10-capable model actually reports in `sysObjectID` — see the PEN ambiguity section above, flagged for the [`ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md) verification backlog. (The newly-confirmed `os10Products` sibling-model list above narrows this somewhat — all S/M/Z/N-series `-ON` models are rooted under PEN 674, per Dell's own MIB; the 6027/Force10 sightings for S3048-ON/S4048-ON/S6010-ON specifically remain a real discrepancy against that, unresolved.)
- Exact internal table structure of `DELLEMC-OS10-CHASSIS-MIB` (plausible `entPhysicalTable`-equivalent for chassis/module/PSU/fan inventory — not enumerated this session, worth a follow-up given SignalScope's inventory use case).
- RMON-MIB is now confirmed **absent** from OS10's own MIB list (not merely unconfirmed) — do not plan RMON-based flow/history collection for this vendor.
